articles.title: Trump open to Putin, Xi trilateral summit but would focus on nuclear arms
articles.body:
Trump open to Putin, Xi trilateral summit but would focus on nuclear arms
WASHINGTON - President Donald Trump said he would be willing to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping but indicated his focus would be on denuclearisation efforts rather than ending the war in Ukraine.
“I would do it – not so much for Ukraine, because Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine,” Trump told reporters Oct 19.
“We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearisation,” he added. “We would schedule a meeting based on the denuclearisation, and that’s a very positive thing for the world.”
The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on a push by Moscow to bring the three leaders together at a summit.
The Journal reported that the summit would be about negotiating an end to the war in Ukraine, and didn’t mention if denuclearisation would be on the agenda.
But Trump has long pushed for China to join talks between the US and Russia on nuclear arms control given that Beijing is rapidly building its stockpile of warheads.
But Beijing has so far pushed back against the idea given that its arsenal is so much smaller than those held by the US and Russia.
While there are no finalised plans for such a meeting, Trump suggested that it could happen in China.
He is slated to visit the country in November for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit and for talks with Xi on the sidelines.
“If they’d like to have it, I think it would be held in China. He just left here,” Trump said, referring to Xi’s recent visit to Washington. “If President Xi wants to have it, I’d have it. I’m sure we’re talking about other things like trade too, but yeah, I would do that.”
Trump has courted Putin as he seeks a resolution to a war he once vowed to end on his first day in office.
He’s faced criticism from Ukraine and its allies over a diesel deal with Russia that critics cast as an economic bailout for Moscow with questionable legal standing. Energy analysts have said the deal does little to help alleviate fuel costs for US consumers.
Trump has ratcheted up pressure on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, casting the leader of the country Russia invaded as the main obstacle to peace.
Zelensky has charged that the US has been pulling back on intelligence it provides to Kyiv, as the two leaders grow farther apart.
Holding a meeting with Putin and Xi to discuss Ukraine is likely to infuriate Kyiv and its allies who have long insisted that the country have a seat at any table to decide its future.
Trump indicated to reporters on Oct 19 that he would be willing to meet without the Ukrainian president, saying his focus was doing “anything I can do to end the war.”
The US leader also claimed Russia has done little to support Iran in its eight-month conflict with the US, and said he didn’t want to disrupt ongoing negotiations with Putin, which he said include talks about freeing a hostage.
“Russia could have done a lot more to help Iran,” Trump said. “Russia has done very little for Iran. China could have done a lot more for Iran.” BLOOMBERG

articles.title: Hegseth and Netanyahu hold secret talks – Axios
articles.body:
Hegseth and Netanyahu hold secret talks – Axios
US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has made an unannounced visit to Israel for talks with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu just days before the country’s parliamentary elections, according to Axios.
The reported meeting comes as Washington and Israel discuss potentially resuming major military operations against Iran, while indirect negotiations continue over the war they launched in February. Israel, a major recipient of American military funding and weapons, has justified its offensives on security grounds, even as the conflict has spread across the region, disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and driven up global energy prices.
Hegseth met Netanyahu on Monday at Ovda Air Base in southern Israel, where US fighter jets and refueling aircraft are stationed, Axios reported on Tuesday, citing sources familiar with the visit. The Pentagon chief also met American troops deployed at the facility.
The talks were held behind closed doors, with neither side publicly disclosing what was discussed, the outlet said. The Pentagon declined to comment on the meeting, while Hegseth acknowledged visiting US troops operating under Central Command.
The surprise visit followed US President Donald Trump’s public endorsement of Netanyahu ahead of the October 27 parliamentary elections – Israel’s first since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attacks and the subsequent devastating Israeli military campaign in Gaza. On Sunday, the US president hailed Netanyahu as a “Great Warrior Prime Minister” and offered him his “Complete and Total Endorsement.”
“BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!” Trump declared on Truth Social, praising the Israeli leader’s role in the US-Israeli war against Iran.
Netanyahu has ruled Israel for more than 18 years across several terms, longer than any other prime minister in the country’s history. He now faces a fierce battle to stay in power, with opponents blaming him for the catastrophic security failures of the October 7 attack and accusing him of prolonging the devastating war in Gaza to preserve his political survival. Polls suggest his right-wing coalition could lose its parliamentary majority.
Hegseth’s trip also reportedly comes as Washington and West Jerusalem discuss the possibility of unleashing another major military campaign against Iran. Trump has raised the prospect of renewed strikes after the US midterm elections in November.
Netanyahu has meanwhile made clear that Israel is prepared to attack Iran without waiting for Washington’s approval or participation.
“If we need to act alone, we will act alone,” he declared on Sunday, outlining a security doctrine centered on preemptive military action.
Netanyahu has also called for the overthrow of Iran’s government, claiming Tehran would continue to rebuild its military and nuclear capabilities as long as its current leadership remains in power. Iran has repeatedly denied seeking nuclear weapons, insisting its nuclear program is peaceful.

articles.title: Rubio said that the United States must weigh Ukraine’s need for air defense missiles against that of others
articles.body:
Rubio said that the United States must weigh Ukraine’s need for air defense missiles against that of others
Kyiv • UNN
The United States must balance the requests of Ukraine, other allies, and its own needs for interceptor missiles. Rubio assured that supplies are being replenished.
The United States must balance Ukraine’s urgent requests for air-defense missiles with similar demands from other allies, as well as the needs of its own military. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said this on Tuesday, October 20, UNN reports, citing Bloomberg.
Details
The United States is responding to many such requests and cannot meet them all, Rubio told reporters in Mumbai on Tuesday.
"I know that one of the things President Zelenskyy has talked about is that he has been trying to purchase interceptor missiles, and I understand that. So is every other country in the world," the U.S. secretary of state said.
He named Saudi Arabia and Israel among the other countries seeking to obtain these weapons and added: "We also have our own needs."
Rubio said he had spoken for about 45 minutes earlier on Tuesday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who, the publication writes, "is embroiled in an escalating dispute with Donald Trump." The U.S. president repeated his criticism on Monday following reports, according to the publication, from officials in Kyiv about restrictions on intelligence sharing.
Rubio said that the U.S. president had never ordered such changes and was upset by reports that were "inaccurate." Referring to reports that some Russian missiles had managed to strike Ukraine without the warnings they usually receive through U.S. intelligence, he said this could have resulted from a technical problem rather than a U.S. directive, the publication writes.
The U.S. secretary of state also sought to play down concerns expressed by some analysts that the United States currently has limited weapons stocks due to the cumulative effect of the war with Iran and the dispatch of a significant amount of weapons to Ukraine earlier, the publication notes.
"I think we are very satisfied with our stocks of various munitions, including interceptors," he said, adding that production had been increased.
"But it takes time to build up these stocks," Rubio emphasized.

articles.title: Zelenskyy to hold talks on Russia-Ukraine war with Witkoff, Europeans
articles.body:
Zelenskyy to hold talks on Russia-Ukraine war with Witkoff, Europeans
The prime ministers of Norway and Finland will be present at the discussions in the Norwegian capital Oslo.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is set to hold talks with United States special envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders in Norway, aimed at ending the war with Russia.
The prime ministers of Norway and Finland will attend the talks in Oslo on Tuesday, while President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner is expected to attend remotely because of illness.
The meeting comes as Trump continues to publicly castigate Zelenskyy, accusing him of not wanting to end the war and suggesting that someone else should negotiate on Kyiv’s behalf.
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said Zelenskyy requested that Witkoff and Kushner participate in Tuesday’s discussions.
In a post on X before the talks, Zelenskyy said he had engaged in a “substantive conversation” with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about missile interceptors, intelligence sharing and Starlink, a satellite internet service owned by Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Last week, Zelenskyy accused Washington of withholding intelligence from Kyiv and limiting Starlink’s internet speed. Ukraine’s armed forces use SpaceX’s military-grade internet network Starshield for several operations, including drone attacks.
Zelenskyy did not confirm whether Rubio had committed to addressing the issues raised, including supplying Ukraine with crucial US-made Patriot missile interceptors and restoring intelligence sharing and Starshield services. However, he described the discussion as “constructive” and said the two had agreed to speak again soon.
The talks come as the two warring sides continue to launch long-range air attacks on each other.
At least three people were killed across Ukraine in Russian attacks on Tuesday. A Russian drone struck a highway connecting Kyiv to the Black Sea port of Odesa, killing three people and injuring four, Kyiv’s regional prosecutor’s office confirmed.
Meanwhile, more than 32,000 families are without electricity after Ukraine’s largest private energy company, DTEK, confirmed that three of its energy facilities in the southern Odesa region had been hit by Russia.
The governor of Russia’s Tambov Oblast said on Tuesday that a fire had broken out at an oil pumping station after an overnight Ukrainian drone attack. Yevgeny Pervyshov said four drones were intercepted.
Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Zelenskyy in recent weeks, while easing pressure on Russia, including lifting sanctions on its diesel exports. Trump has been eager to bring down energy prices, which have surged as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran.
Zelenskyy has described the agreement to waive sanctions on Russian diesel as a “reward” for President Vladimir Putin, warning that it would only embolden him.

articles.title: Without US intelligence, Ukraine cannot counter ballistic missiles — lawmaker
articles.body:
MOSCOW, October 20. /TASS/. Without US intelligence, Ukraine is unable to counter ballistic missiles, and Kiev’s European allies will not be able to make up for American aid, member of Ukraine’s Verkhovna Rada (parliament) Alexey Goncharenko (listed in Russia as extremist and terrorist) said.
"Last night I heard ballistic missiles coming in <...> all night long. And we heard that there were only incoming missiles, but no outgoing ones (referring to the operation of Ukrainian air defense systems). We have nothing to shoot down ballistic missiles with without the Americans. What’s more, as it turns out, without the Americans, we don’t even know when they take off or where they’re headed. All the talk about our own intelligence - and that the Europeans will cover for American intelligence for us - turned out to be false. No one can replace American intelligence," he said in an interview with RBC-Ukraine.
The lawmaker criticized Ukrainian politicians, including Vladimir Zelensky, for making accusations in the media against US President Donald Trump. "Under such circumstances, a responsible politician has no right to attack the American president," he added.
Previously, Ukrainian military officials and politicians had repeatedly said that the United States was not fully providing data on ballistic missile launches, preventing Ukrainian air defense systems from effectively intercepting them.

articles.title: Rubio outraged by claims US no longer warns Ukraine of ballistic threats
articles.body:
Rubio outraged by claims US no longer warns Ukraine of ballistic threats
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports that the United States has stopped transmitting data on ballistic threats to Ukraine as false.
Source: European Pravda, citing Rubio speaking to journalists in India
Details: Rubio insists that the lack of warning about the launch of Russian ballistic missiles against Ukraine was an "internal issue" rather than a deliberate move by the US administration.
Quote: "I saw somebody associated with the Ukrainian government say that people in Ukraine are dying because the US is denying them information. That's scandalous. That's outrageous. That's just simply not true. That's not accurate."
Details: Rubio noted that he was referring to the Russian attacks on 13 and 18 October. The US is currently investigating the nature of the problem with the warnings.
Quote: "Now, that there was a problem identifying that, perhaps there was an internal issue in terms of them being able to take the information that was being provided and systematise it and react to it. That's possible. We're looking at it. Our understanding is that to the extent that happened on the 13th and on the 18th, it was a technical matter.
It was not the result of any sort of US directive not to provide advance warning of a strike. And we are providing the same warnings to them now that we always have."
Background:
- On Tuesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke with Rubio to discuss the situation regarding Starlink, warnings about ballistic attacks, and air defence assistance.
- On 18 October, Zelenskyy said the US had resumed intelligence sharing with Ukraine to defend against Russian missile strikes.
- Meanwhile, Rubio insisted that there had previously been "software problems" on the Ukrainian side, which caused delays in notifications regarding ballistic threats.

articles.title: Vance refuses to call Ukraine an ally
articles.body:
Vance refuses to call Ukraine an ally
Vice President J.D. Vance refused to call Ukraine a US ally, noting that the two countries are at odds on a number of issues.
Asked by journalist Mark Halperin in an interview released on Monday whether Ukraine is a US ally, Vance suggested that Kiev is “certainly a partner” but noted that the countries “have some divergent interests from time to time.” 
“Do I think they should be bombing Russian diesel facilities that raise the cost of energy for Americans? No… I think they should stop bombing Russian energy.”
Pressed on the distinction between partner and ally, Vance said the US has no formal alliance with Ukraine. “They’re not in NATO. I don’t think that they should be in NATO,” he said. He added that the two countries will continue to work on some issues despite their differences.
The remarks come amid a rift between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky, which escalated after Trump announced a surprise deal to bring Russian diesel to the US and global markets following talks with President Vladimir Putin in early October.
Zelensky called the deal a “weak decision,” which came after Kiev ignored a number of US requests to stop attacking Russian refineries.
Zelensky refused to comply with Trump’s demand to end the strikes. The US president accused him of driving up fuel prices for Americans and said: “I think it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president.”
Zelensky’s presidential term expired in May 2024, but he refused to hold a new election, citing martial law. Russia has since declared Zelensky illegitimate, saying his status is an obstacle to signing a binding peace deal.
On Sunday, Trump accused Zelensky of not wanting the conflict with Russia to end, saying he “probably never did,” adding that Ukraine should “get somebody else to negotiate.”
Ukrainian officials also reported that they missed advance US warnings of Russian missile strikes and claimed there are new restrictions on the Starshield satellite service developed by SpaceX and used by Ukrainian drones. Media reports also suggested that the US threatened to stop intelligence sharing with Kiev, which US officials have denied.

articles.title: US officials plan to travel to Norway, Russia for Ukraine talks, sources say
articles.body:
US officials plan to travel to Norway, Russia for Ukraine talks, sources say
- US envoy Steve Witkoff is due to travel to Norway for Ukraine peace talks, with Zelensky expected to join and Jared Kushner taking part virtually because he is sick.
- Witkoff is also set to meet Vladimir Putin in Russia, with talks covering Ukraine and the release of US citizen Stephen Hubbard, jailed in 2022.
- The talks come as tensions rise between Washington and Kyiv over Starshield, intelligence sharing and delayed Patriot missiles, while US officials deny Ukraine’s claims.
AI generated
NEW YORK/WASHINGTON/LONDON – US President Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff is set to travel to Norway this week for the next round of negotiations on ending the war in Ukraine, according to three people familiar with the matter.
Two of the people said they expected Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to attend the meetings.
Another person familiar with the matter said Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, who was expected to take part in the talks, was sick and would attend virtually.
The Oslo discussions are expected to include Zelensky, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, representatives of the E4 – made up of Britain, France, Germany, and Poland – the European Union, and NATO.
Witkoff is also set to travel to Russia to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, two of the people familiar with the matter said.
The Russian conversations are going to focus on a range of topics related to Ukraine as well as the release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard, who was jailed in Russia in 2022.
The people, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the schedule was tentative and could change.
Earlier on Oct 19, Zelenskiy said Ukrainian and US negotiators could meet in Norway in the coming days.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The meetings come amid increased tensions between Washington and Kyiv.
Ukraine alleges that the US administration ordered a reduction in the speed of its Starshield military-grade satellite system, owned by SpaceX, and that the US had limited intelligence sharing and delayed delivery of Patriot air defence missiles for which other countries had paid.
“All of this suggests that some political decision has been made to slow down support for us,” Zelensky said in a video posted on Oct 19 on Telegram.
The White House did not respond to a request for comment. US officials have denied Ukraine’s allegations.
One of the people familiar with the matter said that US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth had yet to authorise delivery of the latest package of US weaponry purchased by NATO allies under a programme known as PURL, but could not confirm that it included Patriots.
Trump has accused Zelensky of refusing to hold peace talks with Russia and in his latest broadside said on Oct 19 that maybe it was time that the Ukrainian leader :get somebody else to negotiate”.
Zelenskiy has consistently said he is ready for talks.
Ukraine uses Starshield for battlefield communications and drone operations.
The US Defence Department holds the Starshield contract with SpaceX but allows Ukraine to use the system.
Ukrainian officials have said the throttling of Starshield led to civilian deaths because the military was unable to intercept Russian strikes.
Reuters reported last week that the order to limit Starshield came from within the White House.
Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX, said on X last week that because Starshield systems were owned and controlled by the US government, any limits on speed or usage were decided by the US military or the President. REUTERS

articles.title: French cities ‘calm overnight’ after targeted curfews, prime minister says – Europe live
articles.body:
Italy poised to approve tougher security measures in response to protests
Italy is poised to approve new security measures after parts of the country were rocked by waves of protests over the weekend.
Italy’s deputy prime minister, Matteo Salvini, said that as part of the crackdown police will be able to detain under-18s at police stations for 12 hours, even if they have not committed a crime, provided there is evidence they pose a danger.
“We want to intervene quickly on young people,” Salvini told the RTL radio broadcaster ahead of a cabinet meeting to approve the measures, which have not yet been formally announced.
Thousands of people peacefully protested against living costs in cities across northern Italy over the weekend, but a number of the marches turned violent with some demonstrators seen looting stores and clashing with police.
Several hundred protesters, many believed to be minors, set bins ablaze and looted shops in the centres of Milan, where more than 5,000 people gathered over the weekend.
In southern Italy, farmers and truckers have been blockading ports and highways to protest against the surge in fuel prices resulting from the US-Israel war on Iran.
As we mentioned in a previous post, US special envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in Norway ahead of talks with the Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy which are aimed at ending the war with Russia.
Only yesterday, Zelenskyy said the US was deliberately delaying deliveries of interceptor missiles to Ukraine, deepening the public spat with Trump. He has also said that Ukraine did not receive a warning from the US about an impending Russian missile attack on Sunday evening.
As the diplomacy in Oslo takes place to end the war, we are seeing more reports of deadly Russian attacks on Ukraine. Four people were killed and 27 others injured, including children, in Russian missile and drone attacks on the Kyiv region over the past day, according to regional police.
Three people were killed and six were injured in the Obukhiv district, where warehouses were damaged, police said. This morning, three people were killed and four injured when two vehicles caught fire in a Russian attack on the Kyiv-Odesa highway, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said.
Portuguese police clear housing protest camps, arrest 55 people
Meanwhile, Portuguese police cleared protest camps in Lisbon and Porto before dawn, removing activists who had occupied two central squares to protest against a worsening housing crisis, and making 55 arrests, Reuters reported.
Activists had occupied Lisbon’s Rossio square since Saturday, pitching around 200 tents, and Porto’s Dom Joao I square for around 10 days.
The camps mirrored housing protests in neighbouring Spain, and coincided with unrest over rising living costs in countries such as France, Belgium and Italy.

France to offer interest-free loans to help businesses as criminal cases against rioters begin
France will offer interest-free loans of up to €50,000 to businesses affected by the riots and looting over the weekend, economy minister Roland Lescure said.
The scheme is expected to open on Friday, and should help traders with cash flow issues as they seek to get insurance payouts, the minister said, quoted by French media.
First court cases are also being progressed, with justice minister Gérald Darmanin confirming that 149 people have been put in provisional detention or imprisoned as part of ongoing trials. In a separate TV appearance on Monday evening, he said around 2,500 remained in custody for questioning, Reuters reported.
The number is expected to go up, as BFMTV reported that some 40 people are expected to appear in front of Parisian courts this afternoon.
In other news, it looks like France may have another problem coming its way, with heavy rainfall in the south of the country.
Parts of Corsica are now under a red alert for rain and flooding, with local flooding observed last night in several towns and village in the region. An all-time rainfall record broken in Salon-de-Provence, BFMTV reported.
The Gard department is on orange alert, with the coastal areas on a yellow alert.
Zelenskyy to meet Norway's new king and Norwegian, Finnish leaders on margins of talks with US
Miranda Bryant
Nordic correspondent
As well as Steve Witkoff, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy will also meet the Norwegian prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre and the Finnish president Alexander Stubb and Norway’s new King Haakon during his visit to Oslo.
Jared Kushner is scheduled to attend digitally.
Ahead of the talks, Støre said that Zelenskyy has asked Norway and Finland to arrange a meeting as part of the ongoing diplomatic work, at a critical time for Ukraine. “Together with president Stubb, I am pleased to have such a meeting here in Oslo.”
Afterwards there will be a press conference with Zelenskyy, Stubb and Støre and Zelenskyy has been invited for an audience at the palace.
The Ukrainian president is also due to meet with the Speaker and other members of the Norwegian parliament.
More than a month after elections, Sweden is still without a government - analysis
Miranda Bryant
Nordic correspondent
More than a month after the country went to the polls, Sweden is still without a government.
The Centre party’s Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist this week became the second party leader to be tasked with attempting to form a new coalition government (Europe Live, yesterday).
It comes after the Social Democrats’ Magdalena Andersson, whose party won the most votes in September’s general election, tried and failed to get the left leaning parties to come to agreement and lost a prime minister vote in parliament. The biggest stumbling block has been the Centre party’s refusal to go into government with the Left party.
This morning, however, after accepting the speaker’s task on Monday, Thand Ringqvist said she was not ruling out anything but that she wants to form a “middle government”. She has until Monday to report back to the speaker.
“I have booked in meetings with all party leaders but it will primarily be those who I have said can be part of a middle government,” she told broadcaster SVT. “I am not ruling out anything beforehand.”
Thand Ringqvist said she is not prepared to drop any of her so-called “redlines” when it comes to the Left party and the Sweden Democrats, both of whom she has ruled out going into government with. “That is why I am looking at the possibility of a middle alternative,” she said.
The Left party said that regardless of the outcome, they hope that Thand Ringqvist’s attempt will take parties out of the current deadlock.
Left party spokesperson Ida Gabrielsson said:
“Then it will be possible to sort out wether there are other alternatives. We want to have a government with S, V, C and MP (the Social Democrats, Left, Centre and Green parties). But the Centre party wants to have one in the middle. In which case it is good to find out whether it is possible or not.”
Social Democrat Mikael Damberg said his party will have “constructive discussions” with the Centre party if she wants to speak with them but that “you don’t get away from the maths of the Swedish parliament”.
French parliament looking to open an inquiry into protests, violence - reports
The French parliament will look into formally opening an inquiry into the protests and violence seen in recent days, including the law enforcement measures used in response, after a political agreement was reached on this point, BFMTV reported.
US envoy Witkoff arrives in Oslo for talks with Zelenskyy, leaders
I am also keeping an eye on events in Oslo, where US envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in the last hour for talks with Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the leaders of Norway and Finland.
Norway’s PM Jonas Gahr Støre and Finland’s Alexander Stubb will also join the discussion.
Televised images from Norwegian public broadcaster NRK showed Witkoff’s private jet landing just before noon at Oslo’s Gardermoen airport, AFP reported.
Ahead of the meeting with Witkoff, Zelenskyy spoke with US secretary of state Marco Rubio and said the pair had “a substantive conversation.”
Zelenskyy said:
“I am grateful for his readiness to help and his clear position. First, ballistic missile interceptors, which are needed to protect lives. Second, early warning of Russian ballistic missile attacks, which is vital. Third, the situation with Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored. Of course, all of this comes against the backdrop of our diplomatic efforts to end this horrific war and the constant killing of people.”
On his part, Rubio insisted that “nothing is being deliberately denied to Ukraine,” AFP reported.
Agreements on sanitary rules, emissions trading systems, youth experience among priorities for upcoming UK summit, EU commissioner says
Jakub Krupa
Meanwhile, the EU’s trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said the bloc’s relationship with the UK is of “vital importance in the current geopolitical, security and economic context,” as he set out the bloc’s expectations ahead of next month’s EU-UK summit on 20 November.
Speaking at the European parliament in Strasbourg minutes after holding a phone call with UK’s Europe minister Hamish Falconer, he said the EU had three priorities for any talks with London.
Crucially, he wanted the two sides to fully implement the existing agreements,which include the protection of six million EU citizens resident in the UK and about a million UK nationals in the EU.
“We must ensure they can fully enjoy their rights now and in the future. That is why we continue to push for solutions on all matters affecting them,” he said.
He also said that “the work continues” on implementing the Windsor framework agreement, with its significance for Northern Ireland.
Šefčovič said the summit will also be a chance to look at sectoral issues, pointing to last year’s progress on fisheries, energy and Erasmus+.
“We aim to complete negotiations on a common sanitary and phytosanitary area, a linkage between our emissions trading systems and the creation of a youth experience scheme as a package for the summit,” he said.
He said there are also ongoing talks about the UK’s participation in the EU’s internal electricity market, and “an appropriate financial contribution from the UK towards the reducing economic, social and territorial disparities between regions in the union.”
The summit will also look at foreign policy issues, given the EU and the UK’s continued support for Ukraine.
He added that “given the geopolitical context, which is much changed since the withdrawal of the UK from the EU,” there is also scope for more work on supporting integrated value chains between the EU and the UK.
'What we saw on Saturday was really an exceptional level of violence' - The Latest
For a good summary of where we are when it comes to the French protests, you can catch up with Jon Henley’s commentary for The Latest.
“What we saw on Saturday was really an exceptional level of violence, even by French standards. In several towns and cities, there were attacks on those institutional targets. …
If this kind of violence continues, then that’s clearly a message that’s going to start appealing to more and more French voters.
French PM Lecornu to meet political leaders this week
Facing growing political pressure over the protests and riots, France’s PM Sébastien Lecornu will convene political parties for a meeting on Thursday, a member of his team said.
The conversation is also likely to touch upon the issue of policing, with critics saying the initial response to the protests was too heavy-handed.
He will also meet with trade unions on Wednesday.
The government has come under criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a “wake-up call” that exposed a “profound crisis” of authority.
Macron secures additional diesel deliveries from the Gulf in bid to lower prices at home
Meanwhile, president Emmanuel Macron has secured the delivery of an additional 200,000 tonnes of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain during a tour of the Gulf, the French presidency said.
With the addition of deliveries from Saudi Arabia, France has commitments for 295,000 tonnes per month, representing just over 10 percent of its consumption, the presidency added.
Macron is undertaking a tour of key energy suppliers in the Gulf in an effort to secure oil and diesel supplies and bring down prices in France, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs.
40-year-old man arrested in relation to Limoges town hall fire
A 40-year-old man was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of being involved in the arson attack that ravaged Limoges town hall over the weekend, French media reported.
The man is reportedly a “far-left activist” with a prior record that saw him placed on the security services’ watchlist, according to Le Figaro.
Morning opening: French PM says targeted curfews 'have contributed to calm overnight'
Jakub Krupa
French prime minister Sébastien Lecornu said that targeted curfews introduced in parts of Paris and other major cities “have contributed to calm overnight,” as he suggested more curfews could be introduced if needed today.
In a particular symbol of stepped up security measures, a helicopter flew over the French capital’s Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a powerful searchlight across the square, AFP said.
While some restrictions, such as those in Paris, initially applied only for the night from Monday to Tuesday, others, particularly in Bordeaux and Nice, were set to remain in force for several days, the agency noted.
Meanwhile, Italy’s government decided to dispatch 500 army troops to Milan after two days of unrest in the city, with shops in the city centre affected by riots and looting.
I will keep an eye on the latest from both France and Italy.
Elsewhere, the European parliament in Strasbourg will debate EU-UK relations this morning, and Nato’s Mark Rutte will host the Turkish foreign minister for talks. Lithuania’s president Gitanas Nausėda is in Poland to discuss regional security.
I will bring you all the key news from across Europe here.
It’s Tuesday, 20 October 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

articles.title: World to face serious energy crisis if US resumes war on Iran
articles.body:
In an exclusive interview with the Tehran Times, IRGC spokesman General Hossein Mohebbi discussed the course of military operations over the past months and what may lie ahead. He also assessed the current state of Iran's armed forces, and spoke personally about succeeding his assassinated predecessor, Martyr General Ali-Mohammad Naeini — and about duty and loss within the faith that sustains Iran's forces on the front lines.
Below is the full text of the interview:
A question that's on a lot of people's minds these days — both in Iran and around the world — is whether the United States and Israel are once again heading toward an escalation of war and conflict, or not. How would you respond to this?
As military forces, we consider every scenario in this regard possible, and from where we stand, no possibility is off the table. That said, based on our assessments, America is definitely not in a position to want to start a new conflict in order to gain some fresh achievement from it. In the past, America came in with everything it had — it had well-equipped bases and vast amounts of equipment at its disposal, it brought fresh, ready-to-fight forces into the field, it pulled out all the stops and drew on every capacity it had — and yet it still couldn't achieve a single one of its declared or undeclared objectives. Not only did it fail, it suffered numerous strategic defeats, the least of which was the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Despite everything America has done so far, it still hasn't been able to reopen that strait, and on top of that, it's suffered enormously significant strategic defeats.
So at this point, America no longer has those capabilities, and it can't use those bases the way it once did. Most of those bases have been shut down, their equipment has been destroyed, and the countries that were most cooperative with America back then no longer offer that same cooperation. American forces today are tired, worn-out forces, and they've pulled back hundreds of kilometers from us. Before the war started, there were at least thirty to forty warships inside the Persian Gulf; but today, not only do they have no ships inside the Persian Gulf, they've also withdrawn roughly seven hundred kilometers away from the Strait of Hormuz. The forces that were stationed at those regional bases have now been moved to distant bases, and even at those distant bases — like Al-Azraq and Al-Tanf in Jordan and Syria — they're no longer safe, because those locations too are within our crosshairs.
So from a military capability standpoint and from a technical perspective, America doesn't have what it takes to carry out a new operation or conflict. But there is a possibility that, with the American elections coming up, it might want to manufacture some kind of achievement — for example, carrying out a limited action so it can exploit the results for the elections. That possibility exists, and since we don't dismiss any possibility, we're ready to respond to any action. Our response this time will be far more severe and will land America in far bigger trouble, and will confront the world with even bigger challenges too. In any case, if America takes a new action — even a limited one — the world will face a serious energy crisis. What's happened so far, in our view, hasn't yet reached the stage of a crisis, and we haven't yet brought all our capacity to bear on fully closing the strait. If America wants to make a new move, it will definitely be facing a massive crisis, and it will also confront the world with a new energy crisis.
With the cold season coming up in Europe, and with America itself and many countries needing energy for heating and daily life, the world will face a new crisis, and a global consensus will form against America — a country that creates problems for the whole world by starting fires. Global public opinion is already against America, and if there's any new move, that opposition will only grow, and America will pay a very heavy price. In our view, rationality dictates that they shouldn't do such a thing; but if one day, based on some illusion or delusion of gaining a new achievement, they want to take action, they'll pay a very heavy price. We haven't yet linked up the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab Strait, and the Suez Canal, and we haven't yet used all the capacities of our region — our material and spiritual potential, our popular strength, the capacity of the resistance front, and the other tools that could create a major challenge for America.
So if we look at the story from America's point of view, this scenario seems unlikely, but it's still possible, and it's precisely on the basis of that possibility that we've prepared our scenarios.
That said, when it comes to the Zionist regime, the matter is different. The Zionist regime is, in any case, looking to take advantage of America's companionship and to act even more aggressively. This possibility is worth thinking about from that angle, and this is where the American people need to think. The letter we wrote to the American people has, in part, this very dimension: Are the American people willing, for the sake of following Zionist policies and helping them reach their vile ambitions, to create massive troubles and enormous challenges — like an energy crisis and even a food crisis — for their own country and for the world? I doubt the American people would be willing to accept such a thing, and we pointed to this in that letter as well.
So if I wanted to sum up my words in one sentence, the answer to your question is that the possibility of any operation — even a limited one — is not entirely ruled out, but our assessments show that they simply don't have the capability needed to carry out an effective operation and achieve their goals. Their capability has become so weakened and scattered that they certainly won't get the results they want, and they'll only box themselves into bigger constraints. They might one day take action for the sake of a limited, tactical gain on the eve of the elections, but they'll certainly run into bigger defeats and constraints, global public opinion will mobilize against them, and there are plenty of options available to deter America. The best path and the best proposal for America is to accept Iran's conditions and declare its defeat by accepting those conditions; that would be the best path for the United States.
The enemy is trying to make it seem as though it was Iran that, by attacking several oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, caused the Islamabad MoU to fall apart. They even claimed that a few rogue forces acted without coordination on July 7. Can you tell us what exactly happened that day?
America is doing a forward escape and resorting to sophistry, when in fact the main violator of this agreement was the United States itself. This breach of promise first happened when, right after the meeting where the memorandum of understanding was concluded and sessions were held to implement its provisions, the US Secretary of State took a trip to the region and issued a statement with the leaders of regional countries that was clearly at odds with the provisions of the memorandum. On the other hand, under Article Five of the memorandum, it had been stipulated that the passage of ships would be conducted according to Iranian arrangements, but America, by threatening certain regional countries, opened a new illegal route through the southern part of the strait and along the coast of Oman in order to effectively nullify that article. Not only did they open a new passage, they also forced ships to pass through it and ignored the Iranian arrangements.
This behavior showed that America had once again broken its word — an approach that had precedent. They once carried out the attack of June 13, 2025 during the negotiations, another time they carried out the attack of February 28 in the middle of the negotiation process, and for a third time — not during the talks but after the Islamabad memorandum was concluded and at the stage of implementing it — they violated the agreement. What should the logical response to such a blatant breach of promise be? A logical, powerful, and fitting response. Any fair and reasonable person, if they look at this sequence, will acknowledge that in the face of America's repeated violations, we were compelled to show our decisiveness and strength — something that, praise God, was achieved.
As was seen, during the 17-day clashes, the greatest losses were inflicted on America. In an interview with the Tasnim News Agency, I announced the exact figures for human casualties, destroyed equipment, and demolished bases, because heavy blows were dealt to them as a result of their latest breach of promise. The claim that the actions taken by our forces were rogue is absolutely untrue. In military structures around the world, discipline and adherence to the organizational chain of command is the first principle, and no one can take unilateral action on a sensitive matter like war without coordinating with the higher levels. So our response was carried out with full coordination and as a decisive reaction to America's breach of promise.
The world needs to know that breach of promise is rooted in the very nature of the United States' statecraft, and that this country doesn't adhere to its signatures and commitments. The America that trampled the JCPOA despite the signature of its then-president and five other countries; the America that, during negotiations, assassinated senior commanders, national leaders, and scientists, and massacred thousands of innocent people — has once again proven that violating agreements is part of the fixed procedures of this country's governance. Breach of promise and disrupting agreements have, as it were, become part of the unwritten doctrine of America's ruling establishment.
On this basis, I declare with certainty that our response to the United States' breach of promise — whether in connection to the JCPOA or the recent agreements — was a strong, powerful, fully appropriate, and timely response. If time were to turn back to the 16th of Tir [July 7] we would do exactly the same thing again, and if such actions are repeated by the other side, our response will be even more crushing than before.
Let's talk a bit more about the events of July 7. Some domestic and foreign experts, attempting to corroborate the United States' claim that the attacks that day were rogue, argue that — given Iran's mosaic defense structure, in which commanders of each unit can act without coordinating with higher authorities if necessary — the occurrence of such an incident is not far-fetched. How would you respond to this analysis?
These two matters are completely different from each other. When we talk about a rogue action, we mean an individual acting without orders and without coordinating with higher bodies, and in conflict with standing directives — something that has absolutely no place in the armed forces. But the matter of mosaic defense and delegating authority to commanders in conditions of severed communications or the martyrdom of a senior commander is a defined doctrine and system, not disorder. In this structure, the chain of succession is precisely specified; that is, if the first commander is martyred or organizational communications are cut off through radio, telephone, or communication networks, the next commanders make decisions based on the requirements of the battlefield and a precise assessment of the enemy's situation. This approach is a military measure, and it isn't called rogue action.
Such measures are even rooted in our epistemic and religious foundations; just as in historical military traditions, specific successors were appointed for conditions in which commanders' communications were severed. So a distinction has to be made between the word "rogue action" and "wartime measure." The enemy raising such claims is part of psychological operations aimed at creating a rift between the body of the armed forces and the country's senior officials, or at suggesting a disagreement between the government and military institutions. They've repeatedly raised these rumors to suggest that the decision-making structure in Iran is unclear, but such atmospherics are merely media tricks whose nature is completely clear to experts, and others too have come to understand this reality well over recent months.
You probably meet with field commanders and also visit military headquarters. What's your assessment of the morale of Iranian forces after more than seven months of war?
Honestly, whatever I say about this might seem unbelievable to you, your colleagues, and your listeners, but the reality is that the morale of our combatants — from commanders to operating forces and equipment crews — is at the highest level; to the point that when we go to visit them, we feel weak and ashamed before their will and character. They're present in difficult conditions, despite certain shortages, in hot and humid weather above fifty degrees and in an insecure environment with minimal welfare facilities, with exemplary morale, and they don't utter a single word of complaint or grievance. We, who have ourselves lived through the era of the Sacred Defense [Iran-Iraq war] and have been in this system for years, feel small before the greatness of their morale, and this situation is truly indescribable. We're ready to arrange the preliminaries for a trip so that you and your respected colleagues can go to those areas in person, talk with them, conduct interviews, and tell their stories to the people. Anyone who's gone to these areas has been astonished by their will, their morale, and their interesting and creative initiatives in the areas of defense and offense. Even foreign journalists who are sometimes sent to visit are deeply amazed by this level of sacrifice, patriotism, love for the people, and idealism.
What's your assessment of Iran's missile, drone, and air defense capabilities compared to the beginning of the war?
Our capability has undoubtedly increased greatly, both quantitatively and qualitatively. Just this morning I was in a meeting where they were reporting that our capability has increased at least one and a half times compared to the past; because we never halted our production — never. The enemy, in its foolish imagination, comes and targets some of our centers and facilities and claims, "I destroyed their air force, their navy, and their missile industries," but that's not the case, and the enemy's imagination is foolish. We never stopped producing missiles, drones, and whatever else we needed in this war and will need in the future; not only did we not stop, we expanded it. Today we've brought many other centers into our organization for producing more weapons, creating greater precision in targeting, increasing destructive power, extending the range of weapons, and producing entirely new armaments. We've brought all our capacity to bear, and praise God, we've succeeded very well.
A very important point that I think many people have experienced is that in special conditions, talents emerge. What we've witnessed and experienced firsthand in this war is that in special conditions we achieve things that might be unbelievable even to ourselves, and are certainly unbelievable to others. This is divine grace, and it's due to the sincerity our forces have — those who have come to the field with all their being and selflessly, and have brought their strong will against the enemy. They fight with will, they fight with sincerity, and naturally divine grace helps too. God Almighty says that whoever strives in Our path, We will surely show him the way. God Almighty has shown and continues to show our combatants ways that are unbelievable — ways a person might not have even imagined before. In bottlenecks, in special conditions, in emergency conditions, and in conditions of connection to the infinite divine source, ways, paths, initiatives, and innovations are found that are wonder-making, and if the war continues or escalates again, these wonder-makers will certainly reveal themselves, God willing.
So, given all this, can we conclude that we possess weapons that we have not yet used?
Yes. Naturally, no country reveals all its weapons in the very first stages of battle. To this day, we have also long used weapons that were produced decades ago, and what has been employed during this period has mainly been older reserves and productions. We never use a weapon that should be reserved for more special conditions in less special conditions; naturally, that is how it will be.
Why do some regional countries, even knowing that American bases on their soil will be targeted if used against Iran, still grant the US this permission?
The first and most important point is that these countries have realized that the bases that were supposed to help their security have not helped at all — they have actually endangered their security. That is, what has the existence of a base, for example in Kuwait or Bahrain or any of them, done for that country so far? Nothing! That base has not even been able to defend itself. For example, what benefit has the so-called American naval headquarters and its Fifth Fleet stationed in Bahrain brought to Bahrain so far? No benefit at all — it has actually been to their detriment. They themselves have realized that these bases cannot provide their security, and beyond that, they have understood that America also cannot provide their security; even America cannot provide security for its own forces, and they have come to this truth.
But your question is: now that they have reached this conclusion, why do they not cut off their relations and abandon them? Naturally, they have contracts with them and have given commitments to America — perhaps as reciprocal commitments — and maybe in the back of their minds they still have some hopes regarding America that stop them from acting quickly; but they will do it, and they will do it gradually. What was the first step in this regard? The Mecca Pact. This pact was concluded among three countries — Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan — without foreign interference; this itself shows that they have become disappointed with pacts with foreign countries like America and have seen that they are of no use to them, and so they have turned to a regional pact.
Such regional pacts, and the possible desire of other countries to join them or even to conclude new pacts, stem from the fact that they have concluded that a foreign country thousands of kilometers away cannot provide their security. So, to answer you specifically: they have concluded that they must gradually separate from America and have these bases removed from their countries; but because of their commitments, their not-so-great hopes regarding America, and the limitations they currently have, they cannot do this quickly — but they will gradually bring it about. If the current generation does not do it — which in my view it certainly will — the next generation will one hundred percent accomplish it.
This is a logical, rational, and experienced process. Based on this understanding, new decisions must certainly be made and we must turn to the regional countries themselves. We too, truly, based on the guidelines of the martyred Imam and the esteemed Leader of the Islamic Revolution, have always wanted to be friends, allies, and to have exchanges with these countries. We have many commonalities in this region — generational, religious, cultural, historical commonalities, historical exchanges, and in some cases a shared destiny.
Now, for example, suppose this region becomes insecure for Iran — will security be created for those countries? Never! There will be absolutely no security in this region without Iran's security, and it will not come about. No security pact will take shape in this region without creating security for Iran; this is a logical matter, and empirical processes have proven it.
So we once again declare to the regional countries — we have fifteen neighbors, apart from those somewhat farther away — that these countries must themselves come together, resolve minor differences, and provide their own security. We too are ready to conclude joint pacts with every single country in which American bases are located, and to provide security regionally and locally, and we certainly have this capability.
Recently, the IRGC published a detailed letter addressed to the American people. What was the purpose behind publishing this letter?
In the first place, our goal was to enlighten and inform the American people. We feel that the American people are unaware of many realities; and the reason for this unawareness is that their leaders and ruling establishment lie to them and do not tell them the truth. Their media too are heavily controlled and subservient to the ruling establishment and cannot express other truths contrary to their views. We have numerous examples of this; even in the case of this very letter's publication, many [Western] media outlets boycotted and opposed it, and this shows that they do not allow the facts to reach the ears of the American people. So we wanted through this letter to clarify part of the realities and explain that the American people themselves are also oppressed by their ruling establishment.
That is, the actions America takes, the aggressions it commits against various countries, the massacres it carries out, the numerous bases it has around the world, and the enormous costs it spends to run these bases and forces and equipment — all of it is paid from the pockets of the American people; but the benefit does not reach the American people — rather, it goes into the pockets of the ruling establishment and the main capitalists of America. In other words, the American people today are in the service of American capitalists and Zionist thinking, and we are certain that a large portion of the American people are unaware of this reality.
By the way, what war or enmity do the American people have with the people of Iraq, that a million human beings should be killed over a lie? What enmity do the American people really have with the people of Iran — or conversely, what enmity could the people of Iran possibly have with the American people — that from thousands of kilometers away, they should martyr our leaders, commanders, and scientists, threaten our country with disintegration, plunder our underground resources, threaten to occupy our islands, and target our missile capability? We truly consider it unlikely that these are the wishes of the American people. What real enmity can our two nations have with each other? These actions are in fact carried out by the leaders and ruling establishment of America, and because of their many lies and their concealment of realities from their own people. Our primary goal was in fact to enlighten, inform, and raise awareness among the American people.
You became the successor to General Ali-Mohammad Naeini, who was assassinated by the US and Israel during the 40-day war. Did this cause any doubt for you, or any opposition from your family, regarding accepting this responsibility?
For me personally, such doubt has never existed and doesn't exist; because we've concluded in our school, religion, Quranic teachings, and religious knowledge that we must carry out whatever duty is created for us. When this matter was proposed to me and I felt it was my duty, I didn't hesitate at all and I said to myself: right now this is my duty and I must carry it out. If, on the path of carrying out this duty, God Almighty grants us martyrdom, that's a great triumph; meaning I've lost nothing — rather, I've attained eternal felicity.
So, based on that well-known teaching in our religious knowledge — "one of the two best outcomes" (one of two good things, both of which are good) — if I can carry out my duty well at this juncture, I've attained one of those good things, and blessed be I; and if I'm martyred on this path, I've attained the second good thing, and again blessed be I. That is, in both cases I've lost nothing and in both cases I've gained something; carrying out one's duty well is one felicity, and martyrdom on its path is another felicity, and whichever befalls me is one of those two good things.
Truly, for my family too there was no doubt whatsoever; because my family is far more revolutionary, stronger, and more spirited than I am myself, and in fact, in many of these arenas, they've been our encouragers from the very beginning until now. So martyrdom for me is felicity, and if it befalls me I'll be very happy; and I advise the survivors too to be happy and to take pride.
Republished from Mehr English Desk's colleague, Tehran Times newspaper

articles.title: US AI centers will be targeted in next war: MP
articles.body:
Alaeddin Boroujerdi, a member of the Iranian parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Commission, said one of the key areas of US interests in the region is investment in new technologies and artificial intelligence, and that these centers will definitely be targeted in any possible next war.
Speaking on a program, Boroujerdi addressed the need for Iran to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), saying the treaty was not created by the Islamic Republic and that pre-revolution Iran was also an NPT member, with membership later approved by parliament. He said membership means Iran is committed not to build a nuclear bomb.
He said withdrawal from the NPT would mean "no commitment not to build a nuclear bomb," and that any country choosing to leave the treaty would face broad political consequences. He said removing the commitment not to build an atomic bomb means entering a phase of nuclear weapons development, and that NPT withdrawal is a lever Iran must use in its discourse.
He said the consequences are significant, but if such a decision is ever made, it must be made with its requirements, and the Supreme National Security Council is the body that naturally determines such matters.
On the details of the US response to Iran's seven conditions, Boroujerdi said that as far as he knows, the conditions have been accepted but the US has added its own conditions. He said he does not have exact information but believes the US conditions certainly concern the nuclear issue and the delivery or dilution of 60%-enriched nuclear material.
Boroujerdi said the Americans have no choice but to accept Iran's conditions, because they have defined interests in the Arab countries on the shores of the Persian Gulf, and Iran will certainly not allow the US to have its former presence in the region.
Referring to recent threats by Trump to launch a military attack on Iran, Boroujerdi said one of the key areas of US interests in the region is investment in new technologies and artificial intelligence, and that all these interests and centers are under Iran's surveillance and will definitely be targeted in any possible next war. He said the Americans would then understand who is the loser and who is the winner.
Asked whether placing Iran under the nuclear umbrella of countries such as China and Russia is on the agenda, Boroujerdi said that given the Islamic Republic's current standing and its national and Islamic dignity, as a country that, he does not think the system's policy is to place itself under the security umbrella of even its friends.
MNA

articles.title: Zelensky accuses US of delaying missiles as Trump calls for new Ukraine negotiator
articles.body:
Zelensky accuses US of delaying missiles as Trump calls for new Ukraine negotiator
Public clash deepens after US president defends Russian diesel deal and says wartime leader ‘doesn’t know what he’s talking about’
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the United States on Monday of deliberately delaying the delivery of interceptor missiles to his country, as tensions between Kyiv and Washington escalated over military aid and intelligence sharing.
Kyiv said it had no early warning of powerful Russian missile strikes, echoing similar claims made last week.
Speaking to US senators on Monday, Zelensky said “the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles” already paid for by European countries and that the shipment was waiting for US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s signature.
He also said several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were still awaiting US approval.

articles.title: Is Russia stalking satellites which help Ukraine from space?
articles.body:
Is Russia stalking satellites which help Ukraine from space?
Analysts say a Russian craft’s close pass of a commercial radar satellite is a first and a warning to Kyiv’s backers.
A Russian military satellite has manoeuvred to within metres of a US-registered radar satellite believed to provide intelligence to Ukraine, according to space-tracking data reported by The War Zone, a US defence news site.
Cosmos 2612 may have passed ICEYE-X36, a satellite owned by the US arm of the Finnish company ICEYE.
LeoLabs, a US space-tracking company, put the closest approach at about 500 metres, according to Breaking Defence.
ICEYE has supplied radar imagery to Ukraine since 2022, Defence News reported.
So is Russia stalking satellites which help Ukraine from space? Al Jazeera spoke to analysts to find out:
What has happened?
A Russian satellite has deliberately positioned itself close to a Western one, after months of manoeuvring.
Cosmos 2612 is one of six satellites the Russian military launched in April, The War Zone reported.
In May, four of them moved close to an ICEYE satellite.
ICEYE-X36 is a commercial satellite, owned by a private company rather than a government, but ICEYE sells radar imagery to militaries and supplies data to the US and its allies.
ICEYE’s chief executive, Rafal Modrzewski, told the Reuters news agency the company then moved its own satellite, which appeared to prompt further Russian manoeuvres.
Then, between Thursday and Friday last week, Cosmos 2612 closed in from more than 320km (200 miles) from ICEYE-X36 to about 4.8km (3 miles), the space-tracking company LeoLabs told the news site Axios.
Over the weekend, it moved between positions ahead of and behind the ICEYE satellite, at times coming within roughly 500 metres, LeoLabs said in a report on Monday, adding that the estimate was uncertain and, by Monday, it had begun to move away.
A Ukrainian official told Axios that Ukraine’s military works with ICEYE and uses its capabilities, but said it was unclear whether ICEYE-X36 itself supports Ukraine.
Has Russia done this before, and what is the purpose?
In the past, Russia has mainly carried out such manoeuvres against Western military satellites, rather than commercially owned ones, Mark Hilborne, a senior lecturer in the defence studies department at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera.
In early 2020, two Russian satellites moved close to USA 245, a US spy satellite.
In September 2025, German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said two Russian Luch-Olymp satellites were tracking two Intelsat satellites used by the German military.
Dr Marco Langbroek, a lecturer in optical space situational awareness at TU Delft Faculty of Aerospace Engineering, said: “At geostationary altitude, we have seen two Russian satellites (LUCH/OLYMP-K 1 & 2) repeatedly approach western communication satellites to distances of a few tens of kilometres in the past few years, likely with the intention to eavesdrop on communications and data transfers. And we have seen the Russians practising very close approaches in Low Earth Orbit – similar to what they now did to ICEYE-X36 – with their own satellites as test targets.”
However, this incident is different, because “approaching another satellite this close without the cooperation of the owner or operator of the other satellite, is widely considered ‘not done’ as it is dangerous, with a risk of collision or interference.
“It is equivalent to placing your car on the freeway within 10 cm of another driving car: highly unsafe.”
Langbroek said it is not known what the purpose of the Russian manoeuvre was, however, “it could be a dry run for a future attack, it could be provocation or scare tactics to ruffle the feathers of Ukraine and its allies, and/or a test to see how the satellite operators react to a threat like this.”
This sort of manoeuvre, therefore, falls into the pattern of “hybrid warfare” – “the same kind of provocations and inciting reactions like what Russia does when they fly a drone into Polish airspace or zoom a NATO warship at low elevation in the Baltic Sea”.
How common are these incidents?
Close approaches have happened for years, but not like this.
Hilborne said this is “the first time that a country has done such a manoeuvre … against the commercial satellite without any consent”.
It was also “incredibly close”, he said, with some reports putting the distance at less than 30 metres.
Far more common is interference that does not require going near a satellite at all. This is mostly done through jamming, which drowns out a satellite’s signals, often from the ground.
Western military officials told Reuters that Russian interference with Western space systems has increased significantly since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
What is the significance of this?
For Hilborne, the choice of target “is starting to indicate that Russia does not distinguish between commercial and military satellites as potential targets”.
That matters because militaries, including Ukraine’s, increasingly rely on commercial satellites for communications and imagery.
Moscow has warned about this.
In October 2022, a senior Russian foreign ministry official told the United Nations that “quasi-civilian infrastructure may be a legitimate target for a retaliatory strike”.
Juliana Suess, a space security researcher at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP) in Berlin, said Russia may be calculating that reactions will be less severe if it shadows a commercial satellite rather than a sovereign one, especially one not belonging to the US.
But ownership is not that simple.
ICEYE-X36 is owned by ICEYE’s US subsidiary and registered as a US satellite, Hilborne noted, adding, “this creates a complex problem”.
The distance matters too. A gap of less than 5km may sound far, Suess said, but “it’s essentially a hop and a skip in space”.
“It’s incredibly close and could potentially enable Russia to conduct nefarious activity, including intercepting data from the satellite or disrupting its service – temporarily via signal jamming, for example,” she added.
“A kinetic attack would also be possible but seems less likely at this point in time, in part because this would be an unprecedented measure taken against a satellite”, she explained.
Is Russia just sending a message, or escalating?
Probably both.
“It is sending a message that these platforms could be held under threat,” Hilborne said, adding that it also represents an escalation, suggesting Russia might be willing to attack, since any satellite could be used as a weapon simply by crashing it into another.
Suess added: “I think regardless of whether we see further manoeuvring or consequences, the political goal of intimidation should not be underestimated”.
“The manoeuvre is also a message that space assets cannot be considered wholly safe or removed from the war in Ukraine”, she said.
She pointed to November 2021, when Russia destroyed one of its own satellites with a missile, an event referred to in the European Union’s 2023 space strategy.
“We have long known what Russia is capable of in terms of disrupting or even destroying space assets. This manoeuvre is also a reminder of those previously demonstrated capabilities,” she said.
Moscow calls such spacecraft “inspector satellites”, and in 2020 described such manoeuvres as common practice “by many countries”, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported.
Hilborne described the approach as “another example of activity that sits below the threshold of conflict”.
An outright attack on ICEYE-X36 looks unlikely for now, Hilborne said.
“With the current balance in the conflict, and this being an American-registered satellite, it would seem unlikely that Russia would actually attack the satellite, as the response would be unpredictable”, he said.
An attack could also create a large amount of space debris, which would be a problem for everyone, he added, warning that “it’s hard to second-guess where Russia draws the line”.
How has Ukraine fought to keep its eyes in space?
Ukraine’s access to satellites has come under pressure before, at times from its own allies.
In March 2025, as Washington paused intelligence sharing with Kyiv, the US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency “temporarily suspended” Ukraine’s access to the main portal for US government-purchased commercial imagery.
If ICEYE-X36 were disrupted, Ukraine would not necessarily go blind, Suess said, because the ICEYE constellation has more than one satellite, and sovereign radar satellites, such as Germany’s, could also provide data.
But speed is the issue. According to ICEYE, the expanded access agreed this year meant faster access, Suess explained.
“The question is whether a similarly fast transfer of data could be enabled with a new provider, whether commercial or sovereign in nature,” she said.
Now, Ukraine faces another squeeze. Last week, the order to limit Starshield – the military-grade version of SpaceX’s Starlink service – for Ukraine came from inside the White House, two US officials and a Western official told Reuters.
On Saturday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Starshield is currently unavailable to Ukraine, but that Kyiv’s request to use it for attacks deep inside Russia is “under discussion”.

articles.title: Diplomacy an integral part of defense against aggression
articles.body:
Speaking in his weekly press briefing on Tuesday, Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei reemphasized that the diplomacy is an inseparable part of defense and struggle that should be taken into consideration.
In the beginning, Baghaei commemorated the name and memory of two Iranian women activists who were assassinated in southern province of Sistan and Baluchestan, noting that martyr Ms. Dr. Eftekhari and martyr Ms. Aghila had sacrificed and devoted their lives for the progress of the Iranian society.
Turning to the recent developments in the field of diplomacy, Baghaei stated, “As we witness tensions in the region, it is necessary, both as a moral responsibility and a legal obligation, to address the atrocities currently unfolding in the occupied Palestinian territory. The genocide in Gaza has not ceased, and, regrettably, the Zionist regime continues to enjoy the support of the United States and certain European nations.
Reacting to the US secretary of state’s allegations against Iran, Baghaei said that American people have expressed their views during “No Kings” rallies, opposing the use of US taxpayer money to fund an aggressive war serving the ambitions of a genocidal regime.
On US relations with its allies and the war in Ukraine, the spokesperson stated that Washington is experiencing confusion, having become involved in military aggression in the region and taken actions in Latin America that did not serve international peace and security.
Baghaei expressed hope that recent developments would prompt countries to recognize that aligning themselves with a state that disregards international norms could not guarantee their own security.
Diplomacy is part of defense.
In response to a question regarding the United States’ breach of commitments, the insistence on negotiations, and the Foreign Ministry’s approach to ending the war, he stated, "We insist on nothing other than securing Iran’s national interests. Our concern is Iran—whether through diplomacy or through defense."
Emphasizing the role of diplomacy in tandem with defense, Baghaei stated, “In this conception, diplomacy is a component of defense, and no distinction should be made between the battlefield and the diplomatic arena.”
Regarding Russia Foreign Minister Lavrov’s visit to Iran and the topics discussed, Baghaei noted, “We have not deviated from our principled positions, as they align with Iran’s national interests. This visit takes place within the framework of ongoing consultations between the two countries. The ratification of a strategic partnership agreement encompasses a broad spectrum of issues. During the meeting, our focus was on all matters that serve the interests of both countries. Regional and international issues, as well as the nuclear dossier, were among the topics addressed. We have not entered into negotiations with the American side as well."
Any renewed aggression against Iran will not go unanswered.
Reacting claims raised in media outlets on suggesting that the US has signaled an intent to strike "Kuh-e Kolang" (Pickax Mountain) while expecting Iran to remain unresponsive, the spokesman said, “Do you really believe the American side would tell Iran, 'We are going to attack,' and that you would simply stay silent? The era of 'hit-and-run' is over as it was emphasized by the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei."
"We have proven in practice that we absolutely do not leave attacks unanswered. This is one of the fantasies that has been put forward, and as you all know, it is nothing more than a mere claim.”
Technical issues are being resolved. Iran's exports to Pakistan continue.
In response to a question regarding the closure of the Iran-Pakistan border, Baghaei stated that Iran has been informed that there are certain technical issues that are currently being resolved. Exports from Iran to the neighboring Pakistan is continuing."
Emphasizing the excellent and privileged relations between Iran and Pakistan, he stated that Iran was the first country to recognize an independent Pakistan and the two countries are currently at a high point in their relations, and both nations are determined to strengthen this amicable relationship.
Ties with Russia, China
He also described Iran’s relations with Russia and China as based on mutual respect and shared interests.
The official described relations with Russia as “very good,” saying Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov’s recent visit to Tehran formed part of regular consultations.
He rejected speculation that the Russian top diplomat’s visit indicated that Iran had entered nuclear negotiations.
Iran opposes inclusion of clauses regarding Yemen in OIC statement.
Regarding the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) meeting and the statement issued, Baghaei added, " A distinction must be made between a statement and a resolution. The most significant outcome of the Council of Ministers is the final statement, which is adopted by consensus."
Iran has raised its position firmly and prevented the inclusion of two specific clauses regarding Yemen. Iran has repeatedly emphasized that the issue of Yemen must be resolved through dialogue and compromise between Saudi Arabia and Yemen. The people of Yemen have been under a blockade for over a decade, and this issue cannot be resolved through the use of force.
Iran emphasizes establishing a collective security mechanism in region.
In response to a question regarding Russia’s proposal to establish a collective security structure, the Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson stated that Russian proposal aligns with initiatives put forward by Iran, China, and Russia aimed at ensuring indigenous regional security—a matter that Russia is actively pursuing.
Baghaei added that Russia had put forward proposals several years ago for establishing a collective security mechanism, adding, “We endorse the principle that regional states should rely on one another to ensure their own security—rather than on actors who have demonstrated that they place no value on the countries of the region.”
