articles.title: UK to deploy fighter jets to help Saudis against Houthi attacks
articles.body:
UK to deploy fighter jets to help Saudis against Houthi attacks
The Ministry of Defence announced Tuesday that Royal Air Force Typhoon fighters will be deployed to the Gulf Kingdom — but stressed they will be only used in a defensive capacity.
A Royal Air Force Eurofighter Typhoon jet comes in to land at RAF Coningsby after a sortie on February 19, 2026 in Coningsby. | Christopher Furlong/Getty Images
LONDON — U.K. fighter jets will be sent to aid Saudi Arabia in defending itself against attacks on critical energy and civilian infrastructure by the Houthis.
The Iranian-backed Islamist militia based in war-torn Yemen has been launching ballistic missile strikes on Saudi Arabia for the past few weeks, successfully hitting three airports earlier this month.
The Ministry of Defence announced Tuesday that Royal Air Force Typhoon fighters will be deployed to the Gulf Kingdom, stressing that they will be only used in a defensive capacity.
Advertisement
U.K. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the “continuing attacks” on the U.K.’s ally are “absolutely despicable.”
“The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region,” he added, referencing the attacks earlier this month that killed 14 people and injured hundreds more.
Streeting said that the fighter jets will be used to protect Saudi airspace from drones and missiles. The U.K. will also send an Atlas A400M aircraft, used to transport the equipment, as well as military advisers.
“This builds on the UK equipment and personnel we already have in the country to defend against Houthi air attacks,” Streeting said.
The MoD stressed there is a link between the conflict in the Persian Gulf and the situation domestically, pointing to disrupted energy supplies and a subsequent rise in the cost of living.
Since Prime Minister Andy Burnham arrived in Downing Street in July he has offered more support to Saudi Arabia. In September, he agreed to a request for air-to-air refueling of the country’s jets.

articles.title: Sudan drone strike kills 11 at displacement camp – official
articles.body:
Sudan drone strike kills 11 at displacement camp – official
Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have killed at least 11 people, including nine children, in a drone attack on a displacement camp in West Darfur, according to the region’s Health and Social Welfare Minister, Babiker Hamdin.
In a statement published on Sunday, Hamdin said that the attack targeted displaced civilians on the Sudan-Chad border. According to preliminary figures, the victims included nine children aged between five and ten and two women aged 23 and 36. Five others were injured.
The victims had reportedly fled their villages last year after RSF fighters allegedly burned and looted their homes. They subsequently sought refuge in Sanakit, near the Chadian border, where they were living in difficult humanitarian conditions before the latest attack.
Hamdin condemned the strike as “a horrific crime and a grave violation of international humanitarian law, reflecting the militia’s indifference to the lives of innocent people.”
He called on the international community to hold those responsible accountable and designate the paramilitary group as a terrorist organization.
Sudan was plunged into a civil war three years ago after a struggle for power broke out between the SAF and the RSF.
Sudan descended into chaos in April 2023 when fighting erupted between the national army, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The conflict followed months of tension between their commanders, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, over a planned transition to civilian rule. What began in the capital, Khartoum, as a power struggle has devastated the country, killing tens of thousands, displacing millions, and pushing parts of Sudan into famine.
Regional and international peace efforts, including African Union mediation and Saudi-US talks in Jeddah, have repeatedly stalled. In September 2025, the Quad group – the US, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and the United Arab Emirates – proposed a three-month humanitarian truce leading to a permanent ceasefire and a civilian-led political transition. Burhan rejected a subsequent US-led proposal that November, arguing it would dismantle state security institutions while leaving the RSF in place. The paramilitaries said they accepted the truce.
The UAE’s involvement has deepened mistrust of mediation. Sudan’s army-backed government severed diplomatic ties with Abu Dhabi in May 2025, accusing it of supporting the RSF. The UAE denies supplying weapons to the paramilitaries. Relations with Washington deteriorated further in September 2026 after the US questioned both factions’ legitimacy. Sudan rejected the remarks and called for peace efforts free from foreign dictates.
Meanwhile, rival administrations have entrenched Sudan’s divisions. Burhan’s government returned to Khartoum in January 2026 after the army recaptured the capital, having operated from Port Sudan during the fighting. In July 2025, the RSF-aligned TASIS coalition announced a rival government based in Nyala, Darfur, with Dagalo heading its governing council. The UN Security Council and African Union rejected the move.
The RSF has faced similar accusations from rights groups over attacks on civilians. In September, the Sudanese Alliance for Rights reported that five people were killed in an attack on a market in North Kordofan, while the Committee for Justice blamed the group for a courthouse strike that killed ten. On October 9, the Sudan Doctors Network accused the rebels of a drone attack on a displacement camp in Blue Nile state that killed 31 people, including four children.
Earlier this month, Russian diplomat Yulia Zhdanova said that Sudanese troops recovered US-supplied weapons intended for Ukraine from RSF fighters near Bara. Their markings indicated that they had been transferred to Kiev in December 2024, she said, according to TASS.

articles.title: Trump open to trilateral talks with Xi, Putin on denuclearization
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday he would consider holding three-way talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, suggesting nuclear disarmament could be a central focus of the meeting.
"We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization," Trump told reporters outside the White House.
"If President Xi wants to have it, I'd have it."
Trump indicated that nuclear disarmament would be a priority in any such meeting.
"We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization," he said.
"We have more nuclear weapons than anybody. Russia is second, China is third, but catching up. China was way behind, and now they're catching up. It'll take about probably five years," Trump added.
Asked whether he would meet Putin and Xi to discuss ending the war without Zelenskyy present, Trump said he would do "anything I can do to end the war, whether somebody's there or not."
Earlier Monday, the Kremlin said that Putin, Trump and Xi could hold a three-way meeting on the sidelines of next month's APEC summit in China and that a potential meeting had come up in talks.
Trump also renewed his criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, saying "it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine."
"Maybe it's time for Zelenskyy to get somebody else to negotiate," Trump told reporters.
"Zelenskyy doesn't know what he's talking about. Zelenskyy is a man that should have had this war settled a long time ago. If he would have listened to me, he would have made a much better deal a long time ago," Trump told reporters before departing the White House.
"I think it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine because what's happened? A tremendous number of people are dead. They're losing their male population," he said.
"Zelenskyy is not helping matters much. I think he doesn't want to stop it, but I want to see people not die."
"We've given a lot to Ukraine. They've given us nothing," he added.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV speaks to Zelenskyy about occupied Oleshky after call with Putin
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV speaks to Zelenskyy about occupied Oleshky after call with Putin
Pope Leo XIV held a phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on 19 October, three days after he spoke with Russian ruler Vladimir Putin.
Source: the Holy See Press Office on X (Twitter), as reported by European Pravda
Details: Pope Leo XIV spoke to Zelenskyy about the situation in the temporarily occupied city of Oleshky in Kherson Oblast.
During the conversation, the pope referred to the request for a "humanitarian ceasefire" that he had raised with Putin.
Quote: "His Holiness expressed the hope that cooperation between both parties will allow for the delivery of food and medical aid, and for the voluntary and safe evacuation of the civilian population. Finally, the Holy Father reaffirmed the commitment of the Holy See to promoting dialogue and peace."
Update at 21:33: Zelenskyy said on social media that he had given the pope a detailed account of Russia's escalating aggression and constant attacks on Ukrainian cities and communities.
"We also discussed the humanitarian catastrophe in temporarily occupied Oleshky. We are working to help our people there. We are preparing decisions. His Holiness informed me about [his] contact with the Russian side on this matter," the Ukrainian president said.
They also discussed "security challenges and threats, including the periodic lack of warnings from our partners about Russian ballistic missile attacks – something that has happened three times recently".
Background:
- Earlier, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called on the international community and international organisations to increase pressure on Russia to end its siege of Oleshky.
- EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on 28 September that the EU was trying to deliver humanitarian aid to occupied Oleshky.
Your support on Patreon helps us keep the news free and accessible.

articles.title: Rubio insists delays in interceptor deliveries to Kyiv are not deliberate
articles.body:
Rubio insists delays in interceptor deliveries to Kyiv are not deliberate
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio insists that "nothing has changed" regarding the supply of American weapons to Ukraine under the Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) programme.
Source: Rubio during his visit to India, as reported by European Pravda
Details: Rubio acknowledged that deliveries of interceptor missiles to Ukraine may be delayed because many US allies are seeking the same weapons. However, he said the PURL programme continues to operate as before and that the US is still sharing intelligence with Ukraine.
Quote: "So, let me clear those up. And as I did in my conversation with him [President Volodymyr Zelenskyy – ed.], number one is the Department of War, everything they've been doing with Ukraine remains the same. That has not changed. Nothing has changed… The second is intelligence sharing. The president [Donald Trump – ed.] made it very clear. He's ordered no such changes. So, none of that has changed."
Details: Rubio noted that interceptor missiles remain the most sought-after type of weaponry in the world, which could lead to delays in deliveries.
Quote: "Every country in the world would like interceptors. And many parts of the world are asking for that. It's probably the most in-demand product right now in the defence field. So when a country doesn't get interceptors from the United States, it's not because we're denying. We have our own needs too…
There is nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine. It's simply a balance between our obligations to other partners and, frankly, our own standards and requirements for our own facilities as well."
Details: Rubio stressed that any delays in the supply of American weapons to Ukraine are not politically motivated.
"I think the important takeaway for you is that there has not been some deliberate political directive to go out and harm Ukraine," he added.
Background:
- On 19 October, Zelenskyy said the US Department of War is delaying the delivery of resources Ukraine needs.
- The president has also accused the US of trying to pressure Kyiv into capitulating to Russia.
Your support on Patreon helps us keep the news free and accessible.

articles.title: Death toll from Houthi attack on Yemen training camp rises to 73
articles.body:
Death toll from Houthi attack on Yemen training camp rises to 73
Oct 20 - An attack by Yemen's Houthi movement on a government security forces training camp in Shabwa province killed 73 people, the provincial media office said, raising the toll from Monday's strike as fighting intensifies.
Fourteen people remained missing, it added.
The Iran-aligned Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognised government, backed by a Saudi-led coalition, have traded attacks since September when the group advanced towards territory near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth.
Local authorities said three ballistic missiles hit security forces on Monday during training. Reuters-verified video showed injured people and bloodied bodies scattered on the ground.
More than 200 people were injured, according to provincial governor Awad al-Wazir.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the camp was run by Saudi forces. Saudi authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Yemeni government forces began a campaign this month to retake Houthi-held areas, recovering ground near the strait. The Houthis are besieging Taiz, the last major urban stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in Yemen's southern highlands.
The conflict has become another front in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran, with Houthi attacks targeting Riyadh's international airport and Saudi Aramco in Saudi Arabia, the world's largest crude exporter.
Shabwa, an energy-rich coastal province overlooking the Gulf of Aden, hosts the Balhaf liquefied natural gas facility, Yemen's largest industrial investment.
Yemen's war began with the Houthi seizure of Sanaa in 2014, which drove the government south. A Saudi-led intervention in 2015 produced a bloody stalemate before a 2022 truce that held until this year.
Aid agencies warn of rapidly deteriorating conditions in what is already one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. REUTERS

articles.title: Who is Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen held by Russia?
articles.body:
Who is Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen held by Russia?
Oct 20 - US special envoy Steve Witkoff is going to discuss the possible release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard from Russian detention with President Vladimir Putin this week, according to people familiar with the matter.
Here are details of Hubbard's case:WHO IS STEPHEN HUBBARD?
Hubbard, 74, a retired schoolteacher, grew up in Big Rapids, Michigan, and served in the US Air Force and National Guard, according to military records cited by the New York Times.
He earned a master’s degree in English and lived in Japan for 25 years where he taught English before moving to Cyprus and then, in 2014, to Izyum in eastern Ukraine with a Ukrainian partner, according to his sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox.
Fox told Reuters in 2024 that Hubbard subsisted on a pension of about $300 a month and had few connections with local people. The siblings last spoke in September 2021.
HOW WAS HE CAPTURED?
Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022 and captured Izyum two months later. Ukrainian forces retook the city in September 2022, but Hubbard was already in Russian custody by then.
Russian state media said Hubbard had been detained in April 2022 and alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint. Reuters could not independently establish the circumstances of his capture.
Fox said she recognised her brother in a YouTube video showing a man being questioned about his views on Putin and the war. Another video showed him with his hands bound, being struck with a sandal. Reuters could not verify when or where the videos were recorded.
WHY WAS HE IMPRISONED?
Following a closed trial, a Moscow court convicted Hubbard of being a mercenary in October 2024 and sentenced him to six years and 10 months in prison.Prosecutors said Hubbard had joined a Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a month. Russian state media said he had pleaded guilty to the charges he faced.
Fox questioned the reported confession, however, saying Hubbard held pro-Russian views and was unlikely to have taken up arms in his seventies.
Martin De Luca, his US-based lawyer, told Reuters in June 2025 that Hubbard had told him the charges against him were false and that he was not in any combat or military unit. He cited Hubbard as telling him Russian soldiers had simply grabbed him from his house.
WHAT IS HUBBARD'S CURRENT STATUS?
In January 2025, Washington designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained, enabling the US government to pursue negotiations for his release.
The State Department has said Russia refused to grant US officials consular access.
The New York Times reported in February 2025 that Hubbard had been moved through at least five Russian detention centres before his trial.
His lawyer said Hubbard's legal team found out only in April 2025 that he was being held in a facility in the Mordovia region, east of Moscow. REUTERS

articles.title: Interceptors, ballistic missile warnings and Starlink: Zelenskyy details call with Rubio
articles.body:
Interceptors, ballistic missile warnings and Starlink: Zelenskyy details call with Rubio
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has spoken with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about interceptors for ballistic missiles, early warning of Russian missile attacks and restoring Starlink/Starshield services.
Source: European Pravda, citing a post by Zelenskyy on Telegram
Details: Zelenskyy described his conversation with Rubio as "constructive".
"I am grateful for his readiness to help and his clear position. First, ballistic missile interceptors, which are needed to protect lives. Second, early warning of Russian ballistic missile attacks, which is vital. Third, the situation with Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored. Of course, all of this comes against the backdrop of our diplomatic efforts to end this horrific war and the constant killing of people," Zelenskyy wrote.
Zelenskyy and Rubio agreed to speak again soon about these issues.
Background:
- It was previously reported that the order to restrict the use of the Starshield satellite system, which Ukraine uses for battlefield communications and drone operations, had come from the White House.
- US Republican Senator Thom Tillis has launched an investigation into the Pentagon's activities over problems with Starlink satellite communications systems encountered by the Ukrainian military.
